mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness, which could lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tighter monetary policy, which could lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates reduced economic activity, which could lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 2% YoY, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply chain weaknesses, which could lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO growth < 2% YoY, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates labor market weakness, which could lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS growth < 0.1% MoM, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which could lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and slowing payroll growth (PAYEMS) indicates labor market weakness, which could lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS growth slows, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) coupled with low unemployment (UNRATE) could lead to monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises and UNRATE is low, this hypothesis is falsified.
